headline: A 2013 law that keeps Defense Department death benefits and survivor payments running for fiscal year 2014 while full funding bills were still pending.
what_it_does: This law provides money so the Department of Defense can keep paying death gratuities and related benefits to families of service members who die. It covers funeral and burial costs, travel for family to funerals and to the return of remains, and unit memorial services. It also continues housing allowance payments for certain dependents of members who die on active duty. The funding follows the FY2013 spending rates and lasts until a full FY2014 appropriation is enacted or December 15, 2013, whichever comes first.

who_it_affects.group: Survivors of deceased military service members
who_it_affects.how: They keep receiving death gratuity payments and related survivor benefits while the full annual funding bill is delayed.

who_it_affects.group: Families traveling for funerals or ceremonies
who_it_affects.how: Authorized funeral travel and travel for the dignified transfer of remains are funded under the law.

who_it_affects.group: Dependents of service members who die on active duty
who_it_affects.how: They can receive a temporary continuation of the basic allowance for housing.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the armed forces and their units
who_it_affects.how: Unit memorial services are funded, and the Defense Department must carry out the law with only the most limited funding actions needed to continue these programs.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 10, 2013; the funding stays available until the earliest of a full FY2014 appropriation for these activities, enactment of the FY2014 defense appropriations act without these activities, or December 15, 2013.
